title: Thunderbird has stopped downloading emails from Yahoo
creator: billdachs
content:
Thunderbird 158.0.1 (64 bit) Thunderbird codename Meadow, Mozilla Thunderbird Snap for Ubuntu-snap-build - 1.0

Running on Ubuntu Linux 24.04

Problem downloading emails from Yahoo

For years there has been no problem, but about 2 weeks ago downloads stopped. Pane at bottom of Thunderbird says downloading message 1 of 292, but is is stuck at 1 and nothing downloads.

Today something different is happening, it downloads the first 80 messages then returns again and downloads same messages again, then repeats. I now have 17 duplicates of these same 80 emails just in the time to write this and it is still downloading the same 80 over and over again.

I have searched internet for solutions. I have done the following:

Updated to Oauth2 through Yahoo website. Thunderbird shows a saved login password oauth://login.yahoo.com, plus my correct email address, plus an OAuth2 password

Checked all server settings. All correct, e.g, pop.mail.yahoo.com Port 995 SSL/TLS security, and OAuth2 authentication method

From server settings page I tested connection to server which came back successfully

Same as above for outgoing server.

I have ample disk space on my computer and ample data capability on Yahoo account.

Confirmed not in offline mode. Confirmed cookies and javascript enabled.

BTW, I can access all my mail on Yahoo’s web page, but that is inconvenient. I really prefer access through Thunderbird.

I have deleted global-messages-db.sqlite and Thunderbird reestablished it. Did the same for popstate.dat, and inbox.msf

I even uninstalled Thunderbird and reinstalled it but no improvement in the problem.

I am out of options now. What to do? Thanks so much.

title: Thunderbird 158.1 receives emails from my new Outlook.com account but cannot send them due to an SMTP OAuth2 authentication failure, despite correct settings and Microsoft permissions.
creator: kbailey69
content:
Thunderbird 158.1 – Outlook.com SMTP OAuth2 authentication failure

I am using Mozilla Thunderbird 158.1 (64-bit) on Windows 11.

I recently created a new Outlook.com email account, kim.bailey69@outlook.com, alongside my existing Hotmail and ntlworld.com accounts.

The problem

Thunderbird successfully receives emails from my new Outlook.com account using IMAP and OAuth2, but cannot send emails from it.

The error messages are:

"Login to server smtp-mail.outlook.com with username kim.bailey69@outlook.com failed."

"Sending of the message failed. Unable to authenticate to Outgoing server (SMTP) smtp-mail.outlook.com."

SMTP configuration

Server: smtp-mail.outlook.com

Port: 587

Connection security: STARTTLS

Authentication method: OAuth2

Username: kim.bailey69@outlook.com

Troubleshooting already completed

Verified all incoming and outgoing server settings.

Confirmed IMAP works and messages arrive successfully.

Confirmed sending from Outlook.com webmail works.

Confirmed my existing Hotmail account sends successfully through Thunderbird.

Tried smtp.office365.com as an alternative SMTP server, without success.

Created a completely new SMTP server entry and assigned it to the Outlook.com account. The same error occurred.

Deleted and recreated Thunderbird's saved Microsoft OAuth2 authentication token.

Checked Microsoft's authorised applications page. Thunderbird has explicit permission to send emails, and Microsoft confirms it was used today.

Checked Microsoft's recent account activity, which showed no unsuccessful sign-ins.

Verified with PowerShell that TCP connections to both SMTP servers on port 587 succeed.

Checked that cookies are enabled in Thunderbird.

Attempted SMTP diagnostic logging using MOZ_LOG with SMTP and SMTPClient modules, but the resulting log files remained empty.

When sending fails, Thunderbird immediately displays the authentication error without opening a new Microsoft sign-in window.

My question

Why does Thunderbird successfully authenticate to Outlook.com for incoming IMAP mail but fail SMTP OAuth2 authentication, despite Microsoft granting permission to send?

Is this a known Thunderbird issue, and what specific diagnostic or corrective action would you recommend that has not already been tried?

I would prefer to resolve this without deleting or recreating my existing email accounts, as they contain many years of messages.
